newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telstra New Zealand to drop prices, expand - paper.
newsitem.headline: Telstra New Zealand to drop prices, expand - paper.

text.p: Telstra New Zealand has signalled substantial price drops for international business customers, the New Zealand InfoTech Weekly newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The telecommunications carrier has created a direct link to its switch in Britain which will then direct traffic to a wide range of countries.
Telstra NZ managing director Peter Williamson said the link was completed two weeks ago and prices would be extremely competitive.
He said that calls, especially to the United States from Britain, were getting cheaper all the time, and those benefits would be passed on to New Zealand customers.
"We are looking to announce some significant drops," Williamson said.

The Australian-owned carrier entered the New Zealand business telecommunications market aggressively earlier this year, and installed a switch in Auckland. Williamson said the company would add two more switches to its network, the first in Wellington, possibly early next year, and then one in Christchurch.

He told the Auckland Chamber of Commerce briefing last Friday Telstra would also offer ISDN services and was gearing up to make them available by the end of the year. The ISDN market was crying out for more services but Telecom's NEC network was unable to offer them, Williamson said.
He said Telstra would offer ETSI or European standards-compatible ISDN, which was different to Telecom's.
Telstra is also looking to offer a cellular service in New Zealand and is understood to be moving close to an agreement.
Telstra and BellSouth have been in discussion about Telstra reselling digital cellular services offered by carrier BellSouth Corp. A deal of that nature is now thought to be less likely.
Williamson said there were a range of options for reselling services but would not reveal who his company was negotiating with.

InfoTech Weekly said it had learned that computer outsourcing company EDS had signed a deal with Telstra which will see all its traffic carried on Telstra's network. That is said to be worth between NZ$10 million and $13 million a year.
Neither EDS nor Williamson would comment.

InfoTech Weekly said it had been told Telstra had been approached by at least one of Telecom's American shareholders (Bell Atlantic and Ameritech) to see if it was interested in buying their shares. It is understood Telstra was preoccupied with its own problems in Australia at the time and declined the offer.
